Arche 3D turns a manufacturing seam into part of the design

Using Aibuild CAM, Arche 3D developed a continuous line-type shell toolpath, with the joining line specifically controlled to follow the spiral along which the geometry develops. The aim was to turn what’s normally a technical manufacturing constraint, the seam, into part of the object’s aesthetic expression.

That’s a meaningfully different starting point for anyone briefing a large-scale sculptural piece, the manufacturing strategy itself can become part of the design, rather than something to work around once the design is finished.
Why we're glad to be part of this

Arche 3D keeps finding new ways to push what a toolpath can do beyond simply producing a shape, and this column is a strong example of that. We’re glad Aibuild CAM gave the team the control they needed to carry the spiral all the way through, seam included, and we’re looking forward to seeing what Arche 3D and Vision Creative Studios do next.

Rather than hiding the seam between printed sections, Arche 3D controlled the toolpath in Aibuild CAM so the seam follows the same spiral logic as the column's geometry, turning a manufacturing constraint into part of the design.

This intelligence layer means what previously required extensive CAD expertise and multiple design iterations can now be accomplished by engineering teams, dramatically reducing the barriers to advanced mould production.
